Veerana Qaid May Baali Sakina Ko Rulata Hai

Hawa Na Roshni Bhi Na

Ussay Na Chain Aata Hai

Wo Zalim Kay Tamachon Say

Hay Zakhmi Phool Sa Chehra

Karay Giriya Bhala Kaisay

Laga Ronay Pay Hai Pehra

Sisakti Hai Sakina Jab

Wo Zalim Muskurata Hai

Wo Zindan Bain Kartay Hain

Sakina Ki Ghareebi Par

Huwey Hain Zulam Jo Jo Bhi

Masooma Paak Bibi Par

Unhe Zulmon Pay Ab Tak Yeh

Falak Ansoo Bahata Hai

Nahi Ab Koi Bhi Sunta

Sakina Ki Duhai Ko

Koi Yeh Ja Kay Batla Day

Meray Sajjad Bhai Ko

Shimr Kyun Baba Ka Chehra

Nahi Mujh Ko Dikhata Hai

Nahi Ab Neend Bhi Aati

Sakina Ko Andheron May

Haye Us Ka Dum Nikalta Hai

Wo Zulmon Kay Hai Ghairon Main

Usay To Baap Ka Seenay

Bohot Ab Yaad Aata Hai

Jo Guzri Hai Sakina Pay

Bhala Wo Kaisay Batlaoun

Hai Johar Dukh Masooma Kay

Main Lafzon Main Na Likh Paoun

Tasawur Un Jafaon Ka

Safay Matam Bichata Hai

/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
p = Path(\"src/data/lyrics/veerana-qaid-may-baali-sakina-ko-rulata-hai-nw-2ff208c4e619.md\")
s = p.read_text()
_, meta, body = s.split(\"---\", 2)
roman = meta.split(\"romanLyrics: |-\\n\")[1]
old = subprocess.check_output([\"git\", \"show\", f\"HEAD:{p}\"], text=True).split(\"---\", 2)[2]
def verses(value):
    return [l.strip().casefold() for l in value.splitlines() if l.strip() and not l.strip().isdigit()]
assert verses(roman) == verses(old)
for value, digits in [(roman, \"12345\"), (body, \"۱۲۳۴۵\")]:
    blocks = value.strip().split(\"\\n\\n\")
    assert [len(verses(block)) for block in blocks] == [3, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6]
    assert [block.splitlines()[0].strip() for block in blocks[1:]] == list(digits)
print(\"Verified all 33 verses and matching stanza structure.\")
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 33 verses in Urdu script and moved the Roman transcription to `romanLyrics`. Both versions have a three-verse opening and five numbered stanzas. Updated the Urdu title and right-to-left direction, and removed the `noUrdu` tag.

I rendered the ambiguous “Safay Matam” as the idiomatic `صفِ ماتم` and kept “Seenay” as `سینے` to preserve the recorded pronunciation.
